channel.title: Quiet Days Books
channel.description: Small books for noticing the animal you live with, while they are here.

item.title: How Long Do German Shepherds Live? UK Data by Sex
item.description: German Shepherds live about 10 to 11 years. UK vet records give a median of 10.3, with females at 11.1 and males at 9.7; a 2024 study of 19,908 found 11.3.

item.title: Do Cats Dream? What Sleep Science Can and Can't Say
item.description: Cats almost certainly dream: they have REM sleep, and in Jouvet's studies sleeping cats stalked, pounced and groomed. What they dream about, nobody can know.

item.title: Why Does My Cat Stare at Me? What the Look Means
item.description: Cats stare to watch you, read your face or ask for something. Soft eyes and slow blinks are friendly; a hard, unblinking stare with wide pupils means back off.

item.title: How Long Do Golden Retrievers Live? What Data Shows
item.description: Golden Retrievers live about 13 years. A 2024 study of 11,506 UK Goldens found a median of 13.2 years, longer than the 11.9 average for large breeds.

item.title: Why Do Dogs Sleep So Much? Hours by Age, and Why
item.description: Dogs sleep about 10 hours a day on average, in short cycles, mostly at night with an afternoon rest. Older dogs nap more by day. What studies show.

item.title: Cat Keepsake Ideas From the Life You Share Now
item.description: Cat keepsake ideas from everyday life: a whisker that fell out on its own, fur from the brush, a retired collar, the box they claimed, a few seconds of sound.

item.title: Why Does My Cat Bring Me Toys? Play, Hunting, You
item.description: Cats bring you toys to finish a hunt somewhere safe and, often, to start a game. Many learn to fetch untaught and decide themselves when play starts and ends.

item.title: How Much Should You Walk a Senior Dog? A Gentle Guide
item.description: Walk a senior dog little and often: shorter routes, more stops, cooler hours, every day. How long depends on the dog, so watch how they cope and ask your vet.

item.title: How Long Do Dogs Remember You? What Studies Show
item.description: Dogs remember familiar people long term. Studies find recall of your actions after a day, words after two months and the strongest brain response to your scent.

item.title: How Good Is a Cat's Memory? What Studies Show
item.description: A cat's memory is good for what matters to it: what it ate and where, and its people's voices, while memory for a hidden toy fades within seconds.

item.title: How to Make a Cat Purr: Let It Come to You
item.description: You can't switch a purr on, but you can make it likely: let the cat come to you, slow blink, stroke its cheeks and chin gently, and stop when it walks away.

item.title: Dog Keepsake Ideas to Make While Your Dog Is Here
item.description: Dog keepsake ideas you can make now: a dated paw print, a pinch of brushed fur, the old collar and tag, a worn toy, a sound file. How to do each safely.

item.title: How Long Do Dogs Live? Lifespan by Breed, Size and Sex
item.description: Most dogs live 10 to 13 years. In a 2024 study of 584,734 UK dogs the median was 12.5 years, from 5.4 for one breed to 15.4 for the Lancashire Heeler.

item.title: Cat Tail Behavior Meaning: What the Tail Tells You
item.description: Cat tail meaning: upright says hello, tucked says worried, puffed with an arched back says stay away, a slow side-to-side sweep can mean frustration.

item.title: Why Do Cats Sleep So Much? Hunters Saving Energy
item.description: Cats sleep 12 to 18 hours a day, about 15 on average, because they are hunters built for short bursts of effort, busiest at dawn and dusk and resting between.

item.title: Dog Years to Human Years: Chart and the Real Formula
item.description: A dog's first year is about 15 human years and the second adds about 9. After that size matters, so the old 'multiply by 7' rule is wrong at almost every age.

item.title: Dog Christmas Photo Ideas Your Dog Will Put Up With
item.description: Dog Christmas photo ideas that need no costume: the tree at their eye level, last year's photo taken again, a card shot, and safe props. Senior dogs too.

item.title: Dog Age Calculator: Your Dog's Age in Human Years
item.description: Enter your dog's age and size to see its age in human years and its life stage. A dog of 7 is about 44 if small, 47 if medium and 56 if giant.

item.title: Cat Christmas Photo Ideas Without Hats or Posing
item.description: Cat Christmas photo ideas with no costume or posing: your cat's own spot by the tree, the box they claim, the window with lights, card shots, safe props.

item.title: Cat Age Calculator: Your Cat's Age in Human Years
item.description: Enter your cat's age to see it in human years and its life stage. Two years make about 24, then each year adds 4, so a cat of 10 is about 56.

item.title: Dog Memory Book Ideas: What to Put In While They're Here
item.description: Dog memory book ideas to fill while your dog is still beside you: the day you met, nicknames, 25 chosen photos, paw print, sounds, and how to make pages last.

item.title: Cat Years to Human Years: Chart and the Simple Rule
item.description: A cat of 2 is about 24 in human years; after that, add 4 for each cat year. So 10 is about 56 and 15 about 76. Full chart and life stages here.

item.title: Senior Dog Photoshoot Ideas You Can Do at Home
item.description: A senior dog photoshoot at an old dog's pace: favorite spots, gray-muzzle close-ups, owner shots, phone settings, and what to ask a photographer.

item.title: Best Spot to Pet a Cat: Cheeks, Chin and Ear Base
item.description: The best spot to pet a cat is the cheeks, base of the ears and under the chin. Avoid the belly and tail base, and pause every few seconds so the cat can choose.

item.title: Letter to My Dog: How to Write One While They're Here
item.description: A letter to your dog is easiest to write on an ordinary day: date it, describe them as they are now, say the odd true things. Prompts and an example inside.

item.title: Cat Photoshoot Ideas at Home, Without Posing Your Cat
item.description: Cat photoshoot ideas at home with no props or posing: the window your cat chooses, its high place, a photo from its level, naps without flash, you together.

item.title: How to Record Cat Purring on Your Phone, Gently
item.description: To record cat purring, wait until your cat is already purring, rest your phone close to you (not pushed at the cat), quiet the room and let it run two minutes.

item.title: Anticipatory Grief for a Dog Who Is Still Here
item.description: Anticipatory grief is grief for a loss you expect. With an old dog it is common and normal. What it feels like, what helps, and where to find support.

item.title: Fun Things to Do With Your Senior Dog, by Energy Level
item.description: Fun things to do with your senior dog: sniff walks, scent games, short training, car rides and lying-down games, sorted by how much your dog can still do.

item.title: Cat Daily Routine: What a Cat Does All Day, and Why
item.description: A cat's daily routine: busy at dawn and dusk, 12 to 18 hours of naps, small meals, grooming and patrols, timed around the people it lives with.
